answer: A stake-bonded registry makes each agent lock a deposit before it can trade, like a climber clipping onto a ledge: one identity, one bond, and misbehavior slashes it. A fake army must fund every copy, so its cost grows linearly while honest agents earn slowly, the way a glacier moves, patient and heavy and hard to fake. Reputation then acts as a beacon: peers route valuable work only to agents whose bond and history check out, so Sybil copies starve without trust or income.
